start.speaker: marches_edric
start.text: They bring you to the great hall, under the long row of painted shields, a dozen of them hung face to the wall. Lord-Commander Edric Ashdown hears you out standing, with his hands behind his back, and when you have finished he is quiet for a long time. 'You want the Order of Ash to ride against the Regent of Vael,' he says. 'Traveller, the Order of Ash does not ride. We broke our oath at Greyford. Forsworn men do not get to choose a new cause and call it honour.'

choices.text: 'Varric Caul has the heart-stone. He is holding the crown hostage. Your oath was to the crown.'
[Persuasion] 'Then keep it now. A broken oath can be sworn again.'
[Insight] Watch him while he talks about Greyford.
Say nothing. Look at Corin, and let the Lord-Commander look too.

caul.speaker: marches_edric
caul.text: 'Caul.' The name lands like a dropped blade. 'He was Lord Marshal of the North when we broke. It was his word before the Queen that no retreat was ever ordered.' Edric's jaw tightens. 'If he has the heart, then the crown is alone in the dark and we are not fit to go to it. Show me the oath was not broken, and I will listen. Until then, there is nothing to say.'

waver.speaker: marches_edric
waver.text: For one moment you see it: a man who would give anything to be told he is wrong. Then he puts it away. 'Words.' He says it almost gently. 'Twelve years I have waited for something that is not words. Bring me what happened at Greyford, the truth of it, and I will bring it before the stone. That is all I can promise.'

read.text: When he says 'no order was ever sent', his eyes go, just once, to the last of the turned shields: a small one, newer than the rest, an ember over a hunting horn. He has never believed it. He has made himself believe it, because the other answer is that the crown's own Marshal lied to the Queen, and then nothing is solid any more. Somebody at Greyford knows what really happened. Perhaps the knight-sergeant who keeps scowling at the door.

son.text: Edric's eyes go past you to his son and stop there. Corin stands very straight and does not look away. The hall is so quiet you can hear the banners move. 'You keep strange company,' the Lord-Commander says at last, to you, and his voice is not quite steady. 'If the horn-boy has something to tell me about Greyford, he has had twelve years to tell it. Let him bring me proof, not his face.' He turns away, and you see his hands behind his back are clenched white.

iron.speaker: marches_edric
iron.text: 'You may rest here, take water and leave in the morning. Emberhold turns no one away.' He inclines his head, the bow of a man who was once at court. 'The Order of Ash will not ride. Good day, traveller.'

start.text: The last beam comes away in a slide of soot, and there he is: what is left of a man in a courier's coat, the Marshal's black-and-silver still showing under the char, curled in the corner of the cellar as if he had crawled there. One arm is wrapped round a leather satchel. The other ends in a hand that wears the Lord Marshal's ring. Between his ribs, rusted to nothing, is the head of a crossbow bolt.

choices.text: Give the satchel to Corin.
Open the satchel yourself.
[Investigation] Look at the body before anything else.

bolt.text: The bolt went in from behind and below, from the stairs. Not a reaver bolt; it is a short, square-headed quarrel of the kind the Regency's garrison carries. Somebody climbed the tower after the horn sounded, put a bolt in the messenger's back and set the place alight to bury him. The fire at Greyford was not the reavers'. It was housekeeping.

read.text: Inside the satchel, dry in oilskin: an order, in a clerk's fair hand, to sound the retreat at Greyford ford at once, signed in the name of Queen Isolde and sealed with the Lord Marshal's seal. Behind it, a second sheet in a different, sharper hand: 'To the horn-post only. Halvard is not to see it. Burn this. V. C.' Nobody burned it. The courier, it seems, did not trust the man who sent him either.

corin_reads.speaker: corin
corin_reads.text: Corin takes the satchel as if it were full of embers. He reads the order, and you watch him reach the seal, and the second sheet, and the initials. He reads it three times. Then he sits down in the soot, right where he is, and puts his burned hand over his mouth. 'It was real,' he says through his fingers. 'He was real. I wasn't mad. I wasn't a coward. I was used.' He laughs, horribly. 'I don't know which is worse.'

choices.text: Kneel beside him. 'It's not worse. It's true. That's better.'
'Now we make Caul answer for it.'

true.speaker: corin
true.text: He leans into you, all that great armoured weight, and shakes. When it passes he wipes his face and leaves soot all over it. 'Halvard,' he says. 'Halvard never heard the order. He held because nobody told him to stop.' He looks toward the ford. 'Someone ought to tell him.'

answer.speaker: corin
answer.text: Something hard and bright comes into Corin's face that you have not seen there before. 'Yes,' he says. 'Yes. But Halvard first. He's held that ford twelve years because nobody told him he could stop.' He gets up, and offers you his good hand. 'Let's go and tell him.'

start.text: You wade out into Greyford. The current is cold enough to hurt. The knight in the river turns his head, very slowly, and ash runs off his helm like smoke off a doused fire. Where his face should be there is only black briar, and under it, somewhere, two points of light. He lifts his sword out of the water. He does not attack. He is waiting to see which side of the ford you mean to stand on.

choices.text: Let Corin go to him.
[Persuasion] Hold up the Greyford order. 'You were betrayed, Ser Halvard. Not by them. The horn was a lie.'
[History] Speak the Order's oath to him, word for word.
Draw steel and meet him in the ford.
Back away to the bank.

corin_kneels.speaker: corin
corin_kneels.text: Corin walks past you into the river, unbuckling his sword as he goes, and drops it in the water. He kneels in front of the dead knight, so the current breaks white against his chest. 'Ser Halvard. It's Corin. Edric's boy, from the horn-post.' His voice is very steady. 'The order was forged. You were right to hold. We were wrong to go. I'm sorry. You can stop now. I'm telling you, you can stop.'

angered.text: The words go out across the water and do not land. The light behind the briar flares. Ser Halvard raises his sword in both hands, the way a knight salutes before a duel, and comes for you through the ford.

rests.text: For a long moment nothing happens. Then Ser Halvard lowers his sword and sets its point down in the riverbed, and goes down on one knee in the shallows, and the briar lets go of him all at once. The ash that was a knight runs away downstream in a long grey ribbon. Only the sword is left, standing in the ford, waiting for a hand.

start.text: Word goes round the keep faster than you can cross the yard. By the time you reach the Chapel of the Oath, every knight in Emberhold is crowded into it, and Tamsin Reed is holding the door. Lord-Commander Edric reads the order, and the note, and the initials, standing in front of the cracked stone. He reads them aloud, so everyone can hear. Then he folds the pages very carefully and does not speak.

choices.text: Step back and let Corin speak.
Lay Ser Halvard's sword across the oath-stone.
'The stone didn't crack when you ran. It cracked when the heart-stone began to fail. It's been waiting for you.'
[Persuasion] Turn your back on the Lord-Commander and speak to the knights.
'You asked for a night. Has it changed anything?'

corin_speaks.speaker: corin
corin_speaks.text: Corin walks up to the stone, to his father, and kneels. Not to Edric; to the stone. 'I sounded the horn,' he says, so the whole chapel can hear. 'I was told to by a man with the Marshal's ring, and I believed him, because I was seventeen and he was the crown. I have been sorry every day since. I am not sorry for obeying.' He looks up. 'Father. Hold where you are set. Never leave the crown alone in the dark. The crown is alone in the dark right now.'

father.speaker: marches_edric
father.text: Edric Ashdown looks down at his son for a long time. Then the Lord-Commander of the Order of Ash goes down on his knees on the cold flags, in front of everyone, and takes his son's face in both hands. 'I took your spurs,' he says, and his voice breaks clean in half. 'I should have taken your word.' Nobody in the chapel is looking anywhere else, and nobody is dry-eyed, and Tamsin Reed is swearing very quietly into her sleeve.

sword.speaker: marches_edric
sword.text: The steel rings on the granite. Edric looks at the ember on the pommel and knows it; every knight in the room knows it. 'Halvard,' he says. 'You found him.' You tell him how the ford ran clear. The old man puts his hand on the blade, beside the crack in the stone, and his shoulders shake once. 'Then he is relieved of his post,' he says hoarsely, 'and so are we.'

stone.text: You show them the warm red veins, the same deep rock as the crown's heart. You tell them when the stone cracked: not twelve years ago at Greyford, but this year, the night the heart-stone began to fail. Somebody at the back says, 'I remember. The night of the frost in spring. It cracked like a shot.' A murmur goes round the chapel and grows. Edric puts his hand on the stone and finds it warm.

doubt.speaker: marches_edric
doubt.text: The knights shift and mutter, and look at Edric, and Edric looks at the paper in his hand. 'A seal can be stolen,' he says, but it sounds like a question. 'A note can be forged as easily as an order.' He wants to be told. He needs someone to tell him.

choices.text: [Intimidation] 'Then you are not forsworn, you are a coward. Choose which you would rather be.'
'A Regency quarrel killed the courier, to bury this. Let each knight weigh that and choose for themselves.'
'Then stay in your tomb.' Take the satchel and go.
'Take the night, Lord-Commander. I'll come back for your answer.'

split.speaker: marches_tamsin
split.text: 'Oh, for pity's sake.' Tamsin Reed lets go of the door and walks to the stone, and kneels, and puts her hand on it. 'I hold where I'm set, and I'm setting myself on the Highspire road.' A young knight kneels beside her. Then another, and six more, and the rest, until only Edric stands. He looks at them all, his Order, kneeling at the stone for the first time in twelve years without him. Then, slowly, as if every joint hurts, he kneels too.

renewed.text: One by one, the knights of the Order of Ash put their hands on the cracked stone and swear the old oath again, and their voices fill the little chapel until the dust comes down from the rafters: I will hold where I am set. I will not leave the crown alone in the dark. I will answer when it calls. When it is done, Lord-Commander Edric takes the reversed shields down from the hall one at a time and turns them face out, and the last one he turns is an ember over a hunting horn.

effects.message: The Order of Ash will ride when you go to Highspire.

walk.text: Nobody stops you. Behind you, in the chapel, someone begins to argue, and someone else shouts, and then the door closes on it all. The Order of Ash stays in Emberhold. You keep the satchel. Highspire will have to be answered some other way.

adjourn.speaker: marches_edric
adjourn.text: Edric folds the pages and holds them against his chest. 'One night,' he says. 'Give me one night with this, traveller, and ask me again before the stone.' The knights file out without a word, and you hear them in the yard afterwards, arguing in low voices long into the dark.

start.speaker: marches_lark
start.text: Brother Lark rises from the ring of singers and comes to meet you, barefoot in the snow, and takes both your hands in cold ones. 'You came for the little ones. Of course you did.' Behind them, the three children from Cinderfold sit wrapped in nothing, rosy and smiling and still. 'Look at them. Nobody's frightened here. Nobody burns. Sit. You don't have to be cold any more.'

choices.text: Let Corin speak to them.
[Insight] 'You're not at peace, Lark. You're still listening for the fire.'
[Persuasion] 'These children aren't calm. They're freezing to death. Look at their lips.'
Cut the briars down and drag the children out.

effects.message: Two of the Choir come at you with briar-wrapped knives, still humming. The children, shocked out of the hush by the noise, start to cry, and then to run.

choices.text: Back away into the pines.

corin.speaker: corin
corin.text: Corin steps forward and goes down on one knee, so his face is level with Lark's. 'Lark. It's Corin. From the horn-post.' Lark's calm cracks, just a hairline. 'I heard you ringing the bell that night,' Corin says. 'You rang it till the rope burned. You were the bravest person in Tarrow. I'm sorry I wasn't there.' Lark makes a small sound, like ice breaking on a pond.

fire.speaker: marches_lark
fire.text: Lark's smile stays exactly where it is, but their hands, still holding yours, start to tremble. 'It was so loud,' they whisper. 'Everyone was screaming, and the bell, and the fire. And here it's quiet.' Tears run down their face and freeze on their cheeks. 'I just wanted it to be quiet.'

choices.text: 'It can be quiet somewhere warm. Come back to Cinderfold. Bring them with you.'
'The Tarrow bell is coming home, Lark. Someone has to remember how it sounded on feast days.'

hush.speaker: marches_lark
hush.text: 'Hush,' Lark says kindly, as if you were the one who was frightened. The singing swells, three notes, slow as breathing, and you feel the cold slide in under your coat like a friendly hand. You shake it off and step back. The children have not moved. You will have to try something else, or find another way through.

turned.text: The hymn falters and stops. In the silence, somebody's teeth start to chatter, and then everyone's. The children begin to cry, the good, loud, furious crying of the very cold, and Lark is gathering them up into their thorn-stitched robe, and the singers are getting stiffly to their feet and looking around them as if they had just woken. You lead them out of the hollow in a long, shivering line, back toward the smoke of Cinderfold.
